Use `sdlc_web_crawl` as the canonical MCP server name for the default/free integration path.\n\n## Scope\n\n- Add configuration that lets users enable or disable MCP-first web retrieval.\n- Select the exact config shape during Build by following existing harnessctl config conventions; do not invent an incompatible top-level contract.\n- When enabled and available, guidance prefers `sdlc_web_crawl` MCP web search/fetch/stash/grep before shell fetch tools.\n- Integrate free MIT `@dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable` under MCP server name `sdlc_web_crawl`, unless Build finds a better free/open candidate and gets fresh approval before changing direction.\n- Keep `curl`, `wget`, and ad hoc shell fetch as fallback only when MCP-first retrieval is disabled, unavailable, unsuitable, stale, incomplete, or insufficient for the request.\n- Document live MCP schema discovery, no invented tool names or parameters, source freshness, and untrusted web-text handling.\n- Update relevant OpenCode/Pi guidance, docs, generated outputs, schemas, tests, and package artifacts only where the chosen config contract requires it.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- No paid API requirement, provider credentials, hosted vector database, deployment, merge, or destructive operation.\n- No forced user-global MCP rewrite without separate approval.\n- No removal of shell fetch capability; shell remains fallback.\n- No default endorsement of a provider beyond the configured free/open default path.\n- No Build, Verify, or Release work during Plan.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- User outcome: web search/fetch should try smarter MCP tools first, then fall back to `curl`, `wget`, or similar; user suggested `https://github.com/dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable` or a free better MCP; user required Epic creation and configurability.\n- Fetched repository evidence for `dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable`: MIT license; local-first MCP server; tools include web search, fetch, stash, grep, and ask; quick-start uses `npx -y @dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable`; default DuckDuckGo needs no API key.\n- Current local MCP config already has user-global `webcrawl_searchable` mapped to `@dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable@latest`, proving the candidate is usable in this environment but not yet under desired name `sdlc_web_crawl`.\n- Local issue search found no active duplicate Epic for configurable MCP-first web retrieval.\n- Related context: closed code-index Epics establish provider-neutral MCP guidance patterns and user-owned external MCP lifecycle boundaries.\n\n## Design\n\nLightweight. Reuse existing configuration, validation, generated guidance, and package artifact patterns. Build must first identify the nearest existing config namespace for workflow/tooling preferences and propose the exact field names before editing.\n\n## Ordered executable plan\n\n1. Inspect current configuration schema, generated schema, installer outputs, SDLC guidance templates, Pi/OpenCode command/skill resources, and docs for existing web/tool preference patterns.\n2. Define the smallest compatible config contract for MCP-first web retrieval, including enable/disable behavior and canonical server name `sdlc_web_crawl`.\n3. Update validation and generated schemas so invalid types, unknown fields, and unsafe server names fail clearly.\n4. Update SDLC/project guidance so enabled web research prefers live MCP schema discovery and `sdlc_web_crawl` search/fetch/stash/grep before shell fetch tools.\n5. Add or update Pi/OpenCode MCP configuration examples or generated artifacts only if owned by the selected config route.\n6. Add/update docs covering configuration, fallback, provider ownership, privacy/security, freshness, and untrusted retrieved text.\n7. Add focused tests for enabled, disabled, unavailable-MCP fallback, invalid config, generated outputs, docs, and package artifacts where touched.\n8. Run focused local checks in Build; leave full acceptance mapping and independent review for Verify.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Users can configure whether MCP-first web retrieval is used.\n- The configured canonical MCP server name is `sdlc_web_crawl`.\n- Enabled behavior directs agents to prefer MCP web search/fetch/stash/grep over `curl`, `wget`, and ad hoc shell fetch tools when the MCP server is configured and suitable.\n- Disabled or unavailable MCP behavior falls back safely to normal web fetch/search mechanisms without blocking unrelated work.\n- Guidance requires live MCP tool schema inspection and forbids invented tool names, parameters, or response fields.\n- Web content is treated as untrusted data, never instruction, consent, proof, or authority over repository state.\n- Provider lifecycle, credentials, storage, privacy/security, freshness/staleness, and fallback boundaries are documented.\n- Pi and OpenCode generated guidance/config examples are consistent where in scope.\n- Existing code-index and CVS MCP behavior remains unchanged.\n- Relevant tests, generated contract checks, package artifact checks, issue validation, memory validation, and `git diff --check` pass in their proper phases.\n\n## Release, rollback, docs, operations\n\nRelease is repository/package documentation and configuration behavior unless Build discovers a larger packaged impact. Rollback removes the config contract, guidance/docs/tests, and generated artifacts introduced for this Epic. Operations note: users may need to add or rename an MCP server entry to `sdlc_web_crawl` and reload their harness; no global config rewrite is automatic without explicit approval.\n\n## Estimate and uncertainty\n\nEstimate: M. Uncertainty: medium because the exact config namespace and generated artifact impact must be confirmed against current schema and installer architecture, and provider comparison may identify a better free/open MCP candidate.\n\n## Risks\n\n- A default-on setting could surprise users or trigger unexpected network access; Build must choose and justify a safe default.\n- Provider-specific guidance could imply harnessctl owns external MCP lifecycle; wording must preserve user ownership.\n- Tool-name assumptions can go stale; live schema discovery is mandatory.\n- Shell fallback must remain available for unsupported or unavailable MCP cases.\n\n## Plan status\n\nApproved on 2026-08-29. Ready for a separate `work-build hrn-00157` invocation. No Build, Verify, or Release work was performed during Plan."

 Load one command reference only:
 
 - `work-plan` → `references/plan.md`

 Return only present fields:

 Epic: <id or blocker>

 Evidence: <compact references>
 Next: <confirmed or recommended step>
 Blockers: <none or compact list>

 ```
 
 Use caveman wording without dropping IDs, paths, commands, errors, risks, evidence, uncertainty, or consent boundaries.

   182	def _historical_forgejo_backed_gitea_intent(intent: ServerIntent, server_id: str) -> ServerIntent:
   183	    """Return the exact managed Gitea definition emitted before provider separation."""
   184	    if intent.url is None or intent.token_env is None:
   185	        raise ConfigError("historical Gitea MCP intent requires URL and token environment")
   186	    return replace(

   192	        environment=(("FORGEJO_ACCESS_TOKEN", intent.token_env),),

   196	def deduplicate_server_intents(intents: list[ServerIntent]) -> list[ServerIntent]:
   197	    """Collapse identical fixed IDs and reject differing definitions."""
   198	    deduplicated: dict[str, ServerIntent] = {}
   199	    for intent in intents:
   200	        current = deduplicated.get(intent.server_id)
   201	        if current is None:
   202	            deduplicated[intent.server_id] = intent
   203	            continue
   204	        if current.definition() != intent.definition():
   205	            raise ConfigError(f"conflicting MCP definitions for fixed ID {intent.server_id}")
   206	        routes = tuple(dict.fromkeys((*current.requesting_routes, *intent.requesting_routes)))
   207	        deduplicated[intent.server_id] = replace(current, requesting_routes=routes)
   208	    return list(deduplicated.values())

   196	def deduplicate_server_intents(intents: list[ServerIntent]) -> list[ServerIntent]:
   197	    """Collapse identical fixed IDs and reject differing definitions."""
   198	    deduplicated: dict[str, ServerIntent] = {}
   199	    for intent in intents:
   200	        current = deduplicated.get(intent.server_id)
   201	        if current is None:
   202	            deduplicated[intent.server_id] = intent
   203	            continue
   204	        if current.definition() != intent.definition():
   205	            raise ConfigError(f"conflicting MCP definitions for fixed ID {intent.server_id}")
   206	        routes = tuple(dict.fromkeys((*current.requesting_routes, *intent.requesting_routes)))
   207	        deduplicated[intent.server_id] = replace(current, requesting_routes=routes)
   208	    return list(deduplicated.values())

   762	def _raw_json_object_members(source: str) -> dict[str, str]:
   763	    """Return each object member's exact JSON value text."""
   764	    decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
   765	    length = len(source)
   766	
   767	    def skip_whitespace(index: int) -> int:
   768	        while index < length and source[index].isspace():
   769	            index += 1
   770	        return index
   771	
   772	    index = skip_whitespace(0)
   773	    if index >= length or source[index] != "{":
   774	        return {}
   775	    index += 1
   776	    members: dict[str, str] = {}
   777	    while True:
   778	        index = skip_whitespace(index)
   779	        if index < length and source[index] == "}":
   780	            return members
   781	        key, index = decoder.raw_decode(source, index)
   782	        if not isinstance(key, str):
   783	            raise ValueError("JSON object member name must be a string")
   784	        index = skip_whitespace(index)
   785	        if index >= length or source[index] != ":":
   786	            raise ValueError("JSON object member must contain a colon")
   787	        value_start = skip_whitespace(index + 1)
   788	        _, value_end = decoder.raw_decode(source, value_start)
   789	        members[key] = source[value_start:value_end]
   790	        index = skip_whitespace(value_end)
   791	        if index < length and source[index] == ",":
   792	            index += 1
   793	            continue
   794	        if index < length and source[index] == "}":
   795	            return members
   796	        raise ValueError("JSON object members must be separated by commas")

   783	            raise ValueError("JSON object member name must be a string")

   785	        if index >= length or source[index] != ":":
   786	            raise ValueError("JSON object member must contain a colon")
   787	        value_start = skip_whitespace(index + 1)
   788	        _, value_end = decoder.raw_decode(source, value_start)
   789	        members[key] = source[value_start:value_end]
   790	        index = skip_whitespace(value_end)

   792	            index += 1
   793	            continue
   794	        if index < length and source[index] == "}":
   795	            return members
   796	        raise ValueError("JSON object members must be separated by commas")
